# 14 — Canonical bytes

*Written by the suite from [`tests/records/test_canonical.gd`](../tests/records/test_canonical.gd). Every line under **What the suite asserts** is the name of a test that runs on every pull request, and its link is the assertion.*

The serialisation contract, asserted rather than assumed.

RECORD_SCHEMA.md §6.4 says records must round-trip bit-for-bit across
platforms and that the decision has to be made before the first fixture is
recorded. Canonical's answer is to quantize on write so that the number the
simulation uses is the number on disk. That claim is only worth anything if
something checks it, and the check has to be exact equality -- an
"approximately equal" assertion here would pass while records silently
drifted, which is the exact failure the schema freeze exists to prevent.

## What the suite asserts

- [Quantize collapses negative zero](../tests/records/test_canonical.gd#L15)
- [A quantized float survives the round trip exactly](../tests/records/test_canonical.gd#L25)
- [The round trip holds over a wide random sweep](../tests/records/test_canonical.gd#L39)
- [Numbers are never written in scientific notation](../tests/records/test_canonical.gd#L50)
- [Positions quantize to a tenth of a millimetre](../tests/records/test_canonical.gd#L58)
- [Encoding sorts keys so the hash ignores insertion order](../tests/records/test_canonical.gd#L63)
- [Encoding keeps ints and floats apart](../tests/records/test_canonical.gd#L71)
- [Encoding has no whitespace](../tests/records/test_canonical.gd#L78)
- [The hash is sixty four hex characters](../tests/records/test_canonical.gd#L84)
- [The unset hash means no simulation has run](../tests/records/test_canonical.gd#L91)
- [A changed value changes the hash](../tests/records/test_canonical.gd#L99)
